limitations_and_boundaries: CellOT generalization to unseen patients or settings requires similar unperturbed samples and perturbation responses in the training set.
CellOT performance drops when perturbations are too strong (distributions before and after are very different) or when cell types are sparsely represented.
The method assumes deterministic trajectories and may benefit from future probabilistic extensions.
Evaluation was performed on relatively small datasets; large-scale cohort studies are needed for further validation.

research_questions.statement: How can we learn single-cell perturbation responses from unpaired control and perturbed cell populations?

evidence_spans.content: CellOT is a framework for learning the response of individual cells to a given perturbation by mapping unpaired distributions using neural optimal transport.

provenance.text_excerpt: Here we leverage the theory of optimal transport and the recent advent of input convex neural architectures to present CellOT, a framework for learning the response of individual cells to a given perturbation by mapping these unpaired distributions.

methods.name: CellOT
methods.protocol_description: CellOT learns an optimal transport map for each perturbation by parameterizing convex potentials of the dual optimal transport problem using input convex neural networks. The optimal map Tk is recovered as the gradient of a convex function gk (∇gk). Training is performed on unperturbed control population ρc and perturbed population ρk. The map Tk is then applied to unseen control cells to predict perturbed states.
